title: Letter and Portrait
premise: When the coffin of Aldous Vane, founder of the coastal town of Marrow Bay, is exhumed for a centennial reburial and found empty, retired detective Petra Eastwick is dragged back into investigative work by a young constable who idolizes him. Petra discovers a century-old letter hidden in his late aunt's estate that suggests Vane never died in 1924 — and that someone in town has been guarding that secret across generations, killing to keep it buried. As Petra traces the letter's authorship through the town's founding families, he realizes the killer is using the original case file as a script, staging each new death to mirror an unsolved disappearance from 1924. In the end Petra traps the killer — the town archivist, Vane's own great-granddaughter, who has spent her life protecting the family myth — and chooses loyalty over silence by publishing the truth, finally earning his place in the community he'd kept at arm's length.
about_author: Odile Hartwell is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing small-town records before turning to crime fiction full time. She writes from a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage on the Atlantic coast, where she collects antique letters and photographs.

chapters.title: The Weight of Empty Paper
chapters.summary: Petra Eastwick's POV. In his failing bookshop, Petra catalogs his late aunt's estate and finds a sealed letter dated 1924 among her papers, addressed to 'whoever digs me up.' He almost throws it away; instead he pockets it. Emotional beat: restless grief and the itch of an old instinct waking.

chapters.title: A Centennial Invitation
chapters.summary: Constable Imogen Reyes visits the shop with tickets to the exhumation of town founder Aldous Vane, part of Marrow Bay's centennial festival. She admires Petra openly; he deflects. The letter burns in his pocket. Emotional beat: reluctant connection, the pull of belonging he keeps refusing.

chapters.title: What the Ground Gave Back
chapters.summary: Third-person limited on Imogen. At the cemetery, the coffin is opened before two hundred townsfolk: it holds only stones and a rotted coat. Gasps, cameras, the mayor's frozen smile. Petra watches the crowd rather than the grave — and sees one face go white. Emotional beat: public shock masking private terror.

chapters.title: The Man Who Knew Too Neatly
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The police flounder; the mayor quietly asks Petra to consult. Reviewing the 1924 file, he notices the death certificate was signed by a doctor who died a week later. Someone has handled this file recently — the paper smells of modern preservative. Emotional beat: the old competence returning like a second language.

chapters.title: Ink Older Than Lies
chapters.summary: Petra opens his aunt's letter at last: written in Vane's hand, it says 'I am not dead, and three people helped me vanish.' One name is smudged; another is recognizable — the ancestor of the current town archivist, Marguerite Vane. Emotional beat: vertigo as history rewrites itself.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Perfect Memory
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. In the town archive, Marguerite fields Petra's questions with flawless charm, steering him away from 1924. Alone afterward, she unlocks a hidden drawer and reads a matching letter of her own. Emotional beat: poised menace; we learn she knows more than any investigator.

chapters.title: First Stone, First Blood
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. A retired gravedigger who worked the centennial preparations is found drowned in the flooded quarry, staged exactly like a 1924 drowning the file calls 'accidental.' Petra recognizes the staging instantly. Emotional beat: dread hardening into certainty — a killer is performing the file.

chapters.title: Reading a Killer's Library
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. He maps the murders against the file page by page and predicts the next staged death: a poisoning mimicking the 'fever' that killed Vane's business partner. He begs the chief to act on a prediction; they refuse. Emotional beat: frustration of the prophet nobody believes.

chapters.title: Tea with Ghosts
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite hosts Petra for tea, probing what he knows about the letter while offering curated archives. Their duel is entirely subtextual. Afterward she burns one document. Emotional beat: cat-and-mouse intimacy; both leave believing they're ahead.

chapters.title: The Poisoner's Page
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. Despite precautions, the mayor's rival dies of arsenic at the festival banquet — precisely as predicted. Public panic; the chief finally deputizes Petra fully. Imogen catches him lying about where he was that night. Emotional beat: vindication shadowed by suspicion falling on Petra himself.

chapters.title: Suspect in His Own Shop
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A leaked tip makes Petra the prime suspect: the anonymous caller quoted the 1924 file verbatim, something only investigators could do. His shop is searched; his aunt's letter nearly seized. Emotional beat: isolation — the outsider again, betrayed by the town he's trying to save.

chapters.title: Imogen's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. Ordered to surveil Petra, Imogen instead finds evidence clearing him — but reporting it means admitting she disobeyed orders. She chooses truth over career and tells the chief. Emotional beat: loyalty tested between institution and conscience; found-family bond cementing.

chapters.title: The Smudged Name
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Using ultraviolet imaging on the letter, Petra recovers the smudged name: not a person but a place — the Vane house, now the historical museum Marguerite curates. He realizes the vanishing was orchestrated from inside the family. Emotional beat: the map finally resolving.

chapters.title: Beneath the Museum Floor
chapters.summary: Imogen and Petra break into the museum after hours and find a sealed room beneath the floorboards: Aldous Vane's actual remains, a second coffin, and decades of forged documents maintaining the death myth. They are discovered — by Marguerite, holding a shotgun. Emotional beat: revelation colliding with mortal danger.

chapters.title: Confession at Gunpoint
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Cornered, Marguerite tells her story: Vane faked his death to escape a murder charge, and every generation of her family has killed to keep the legend — and the family fortune — intact. She offers Petra a choice: join the keepers of the secret or disappear like the others. Emotional beat: chilling sincerity; evil as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Long Night in the Museum
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Held overnight, Petra stalls with questions, learning the final staged murder is planned for the centennial closing ceremony — the 'return of the founder.' He signals Imogen through a broken transom using bookshop code from chapter two. Emotional beat: patience as weapon; trust paying off.

chapters.title: Ceremony of Ashes
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. At the ceremony, the town gathers to rebury an empty coffin. Petra, released under watch, publicly announces that Vane's real body has been found — forcing the killer's hand early. The crowd's murmur becomes a roar. Emotional beat: gambit; truth detonated in daylight.

chapters.title: Chase Through the Founders' Streets
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Marguerite flees through the festival crowds toward the sea caves where Vane once hid, with Petra and Imogen pursuing. She nearly escapes by boat but returns — unable to abandon the family letters burning in her satchel. Emotional beat: kinetic climax; myth proving heavier than freedom.

chapters.title: The Cave Where It Began
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. In the cave, Marguerite, cornered, nearly kills Petra but hesitates when he addresses her not as a monster but as the last loyal daughter of a lie. Imogen takes her into custody unharmed. Emotional beat: mercy as victory; the cycle breaking.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. In custody, Marguerite confesses everything in a statement so complete it reads like an archive itself. She asks only that the true history be preserved alongside the myth. Petra agrees. Emotional beat: bleak dignity; the keeper of secrets becoming their witness.

chapters.title: Reburial
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Months later, Vane's real remains are buried with honest inscriptions, and the town absorbs its corrected history — some grateful, some furious. Petra donates his aunt's letter to the archive, co-curation offered to him. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not granted.

chapters.title: Open Sign
chapters.summary: Petra and Imogen's shared POV coda. The bookshop thrives; Imogen studies for her detective's exam with Petra as mentor. A stranger leaves a mysterious old letter on the counter — a hook, gently closed. Emotional beat: warmth, continuity, and the promise that stories — and cases — never truly end.
